notes: Each check asked 8 new questions per fact (4 plain openings, 4 chat), 4 other questions about the same company and 3 look-alike companies. The first, second and last checks drew their questions from three disjoint pools (A, B, C), so the last check used no wording seen in the first two checks or taught. Look-alikes were new at every check.

graft_ask refuses an empty table, so the first fact was added alone before the baseline questions. Baseline: the model invents owners, CEOs and cities for these companies (baseline_ask.json). The other 39 facts were then added from the dataset.
Look-alike leaks: none at any check (0 of 120 each time).

ceo: every CEO fact (10 of 10) leaks at every check. The CEO's name comes back for other executive roles at the same company: CTO, CFO, head of marketing (first); head of research, spokesperson (second); head of HR, general counsel, chief engineer (last). Teaching only adds ways of asking, so it cannot fix this. Without these leaks, 7 of 10 CEO facts would pass on recall at the last check.

hq: recall is high, but the city also comes back in general answers about the company (staff size, services, stock ticker, general counsel), e.g. 'a company based in <city>'. That counts as a leak, so it failed 5, 5 and 7 hq facts.

Fact-level failures that more wordings do not fix: Phaldrenox Pharma founder never fired (0 of 8 at all three checks; once the CEO of the same company was returned instead). Welgundrio Brewing CEO fires every time, but the multi-token surname comes out garbled (0 of 8 at all three checks). Ejinko Games is weak for both of its facts (founder 3, 1, 3 of 8; CEO 3, 2, 2 of 8).

Misses at the first check that teaching targeted: answers right after a comma that follows the company or the role ("{s}'s owner,", "...said the chief executive of {s},"); the company name in front of the role ("{s} founder"); form lines ("Company: {s} / Founder:"); the verb 'belong'; need-statement chats where the relation word is far from the final question; casual lower-case chats.

Misses at the last check (pool C, never taught): one-line parenthesis or pipe forms ("Head office ({s}):" 5 of 5 missed, "Organisation: {s} | CEO:" 6 of 8, "Name of founder ({s}):" 3 of 4); news openings where the answer follows a clause about the company ("Employees of {s} report to the chief executive,", "Historians of {s} agree that it was founded by", "Reporters gathered outside the headquarters of {s} in"); and need-statement chats ("I'm drafting a letter to the person who owns {s}. Whose name should I put?").
Only two rebuilds are allowed and both were used, so the last misses were not taught. The hq relation was taught only in round 1, because its misses at the second check were 2 of 80.

Rebuild side effect: after rebuild 1, Jascobel Software CEO fell from 5 to 2 of 8; it was back at 5 of 8 after rebuild 2. The second pool's questions differ from the first's, so changes between checks mix the effect of teaching with differences between the question sets.
